report.source_text: Laboratory tests yielded the following results: normal coagulation function, blood glucose, routine urine tests, routine stool tests, electrocardiography and chest radiography. The screening result for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) antibody was negative. Quantitative analysis of HBV DNA yielded a value of 4.18 × 105 IU/mL. Routine blood examination revealed an elevated white blood cell count of 10.84 × 109/L. CRP was 20.8 mg/L. ALT and serum creatinine were slightly elevated at 54 U/L and 138 µmol/L, respectively. Color ultrasonography showed multiple hepatic cysts and renal cysts.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man presented with a five-week history of right facial erythema, clustered blisters, severe pain, and upper right jaw tooth exfoliation following an initial diagnosis of acute periodontitis and herpes zoster (HZ). Physical examination revealed pigmentation, scars on the right face, loss of crowns of multiple teeth, gingival recession, and alveolar bone exposure in the right maxillary arch. Imaging (panoramic radiograph and CT) demonstrated decreased bone density, poor alveolar socket healing, and empty tooth sockets in the right maxilla. Histopathology of the exposed bone showed fibrinoid necrosis of vascular walls, necrotic lamellar bone devoid of osteoblasts and osteocytes, neutrophilic infiltration, and bacterial aggregates, consistent with alveolar osteonecrosis. Laboratory tests excluded other infectious etiologies and systemic causes, with normal coagulation, negative HIV, elevated inflammatory markers, and detectable HBV DNA.

Imaging revealed decreased bone density, poor socket healing, and empty tooth sockets on the right maxilla
Histopathology revealed necrotic bone devoid of osteoblasts and osteocytes, fibrinoid necrosis of vessels, and inflammatory infiltration
Laboratory tests excluded HIV and other systemic causes; elevated WBC and CRP indicated inflammation; HBV DNA detected
